turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): hey. doctor ellis is stuck on a note, she'll be in. what should i stick on the chart?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): um, my legs. they creep at night and i can't sleep. oh, the cuff at the pharmacy said my pulse was 96. i don't know if you even need that.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): 96, i'll recheck in a sec. your husband did the intake. he wrote you skip the iron on sundays, and a little cut on your finger healed in five days.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): sundays? no. it's saturdays i skip it. and that cut healed fine, i don't know why he put it on there.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): okay, saturdays. pulse on my monitor is 96, same as you said. blood pressure 122 over 78.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): sorry, this computer keeps jumping. say again why you came?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): the creeping in my legs at night. i barely sleep.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): mm. how long's the creeping been going on?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): i don't know, doctor. maybe two weeks. or three. i really can't say when it started.
[SEG0010] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): the midwife note says about six weeks of the leg creeping, just so it's in the room.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): six? i don't think so. it feels newer than that.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): alright, somewhere between two and six weeks. i'm not making you two match it. which leg?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): mostly the left, and it's every night. both a bit, but the left is worse. it comes on when i lie down.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): sleep, every night or just some nights?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): pretty much every night. i wake up and they're going. ugh, and the garage was a mess, that's why i was late.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): you're fine. any pain in the legs, any swelling, a calf that feels hot?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): no pain. no swelling. they don't feel hot. i checked, i don't know, doctor.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): headaches? vision different? any contractions?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): no headaches. vision's the same. no contractions. i'm 30 weeks, they said.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): right, thirty weeks. stomach, bowels, that whole system, anything going on?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): no. stomach's okay. bowels too.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): medicines. slow, i'm typing and the screen's lagging.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): folic acid, one milligram, every morning, for the pregnancy. and the iron, feros sulfate, 325 milligrams, once a day, except saturdays.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): hold on, the iron name and dose again? it wiped.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): ferrous sulfate. 325 milligrams. once a day, not on saturday.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): anything you stopped, or got told to take and never did?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): i stopped the magnesium in march. magnesium oxide, 400 milligrams. it gave me the runs. somebody said colace but i never took that, not once.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): that cut from the intake, any wounds that heal slow? and any allergies, medicines or food?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): no. it healed in five days, totally normal. no allergies. nothing i react to.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): family, your mom, restless legs or clots?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): my mom has restless legs. clots i don't know, doctor. i don't think so.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): you smoking? drinking?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): i quit smoking when i found out. i don't drink at all now.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): quick look. left calf isn't red, isn't swollen. both ankles are soft. pulses are there in both feet.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): thinking out loud, could be low iron, could just be thirty weeks, restless legs is on that list. i'm not calling it any of those yet. let's see what the ferritin says before i land anywhere.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): they told me the old ferritin was low, like eleven or something. i don't remember the real number.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): yeah i'm not using eleven-ish. thursday morning the nurse takes bloods, ferritin and a blood count, eight thirty. nothing to eat after midnight, water's okay, and take your iron after the draw, not before.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): thursday, eight thirty. um is the midwife visit still happening? i don't know the day.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): it's booked. midwife check in two weeks, and i'll see you at that same visit. if the ferritin and the count are borderline we do a third test, an iron panel. not ordering that now.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): if the creeping does not settle after we sort the iron, then a scan of the leg veins. only if it doesn't settle. keep the folic acid and the iron, and try not to skip saturdays. dose stays the same.
[SEG0041] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): i'll put you down thursday morning, 8:30, for the ferritin and the blood count. slip will be at the desk.

spec.situation: Pregnant woman at 30 weeks with creeping legs at night and poor sleep; ferritin discussed; takes folic acid and iron; midwife check booked.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: No family history of clots was elicited as uncertain/negative leaning: patient said she did not think so.
Stopped magnesium oxide 400 mg in March because it caused diarrhea/'the runs'.
Colace was suggested but the patient never took it, not once.
Patient reported a prior ferritin was low, 'like eleven or something,' though she did not remember the exact number.
